body:
### Summary

I have a workspace project with several child members (defined via tools.uv.workspace.members = ["shared/*"].

In one of the child projects I have a tools.uv.package = true and a [package.scripts] section.  This project is also a dependency of the root workspace (to ensure it is installed" on sync).

however when I run uv sync it spits out a warning.

```
warning: Skipping installation of entry points (`project.scripts`) for package `ccaas-data-tables` because this project is not packaged; to install entry points, set `tool.uv.package = true` or define a `build-system`
```

even though it actually builds the script in .venv/bin

root pyproject
```toml
[project]
name = "my-project"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = "~=3.11.0"
dependencies = [
    "ccaas-data-tables",
]

[tool.uv.workspace]
members = ["shared/*"]

[tool.uv.sources]
ccaas-data-tables = { workspace = true }

```

Child pyproject
```toml
[project]
name = "ccaas-data-tables"
version = "0.1.0"
dependencies = [
    "click~=8.5.0",
]

[tools.uv]
package = true

[project.scripts]
my_script = "my_script:cli"
```

### Platform

macOS 15.7.9 (Darwin 24.6.0 x86_64)

### Version

uv 0.12.3 (x86_64-apple-darwin)

### Python version

Python 3.11.13
title: uv sync produces incorrect warning about entry points (project.scripts) in a child package within a workspace
